seo.title: AB InBev BEES Ads: AI-driven retail media network on a B2B super app - 3.9M MAU, $52.5B GMV (2025)
seo.meta_description: AB InBev turns its BEES ordering super app into a retail media network with Topsort: automated auction, AI targeting by retailer profile, self-service for brands. 3.9M MAU, $52.5B GMV.
seo.resume_citable: AB InBev turned its B2B ordering super app BEES (3.9 million monthly active users, $52.5 billion in GMV in 2025, 29 markets) into a retail media network, BEES Ads, built on Topsort's infrastructure: each sponsored placement is auctioned and targeted on the retailer's profile and purchase history, with third-party brands running their campaigns self-service.

faq.a: BEES Ads is AB InBev's retail media network, grafted onto its B2B ordering super app BEES. Built on Topsort's infrastructure, it inserts sponsored placements into the app's purchase journey, targeted on the retailer's profile and purchase history, and lets brands manage their campaigns self-service with auction-based billing (payment for the ads that are displayed).

faq.q: What is the scale of the setup?
faq.a: The network relies on the BEES super app audience: 3.9 million monthly active users. The BEES platform generated $52.5 billion in GMV in 2025 (up 12%) and was live in 29 markets as of December 31, with 72% of group revenue captured through B2B digital platforms.

Level B. The advertising mechanics (auction, AI targeting, self-service) are documented by a quantified case study from the vendor Topsort, and the scale of the foundation is corroborated by established press reporting AB InBev's 2025 annual results. No advertising revenue specific to BEES Ads is broken out publicly, and no precise launch date has been disclosed.

pattern: retail media network on a B2B super app: automated auction and AI personalization of sponsored placements based on the retailer's profile, self-service for third-party brands
etape_parcours: monetization of the B2B audience (advertiser-side upstream: retail media buying)
objectif_business: Monetize the captive retailer audience of the BEES super app by turning it into a retail media network. AB InBev, a manufacturer and distributor, becomes a seller of advertising space on its own ordering channel: brands (its own and third parties) buy sponsored placements targeted at the retailers already reordering on the platform. Monetization is added on top of existing GMV, with no extra audience acquisition cost.
description: BEES is AB InBev's B2B super app: retailers (grocery stores, bars, points of sale) use it to order and restock. AB InBev grafted a retail media network onto this channel, BEES Ads, built on Topsort's advertising infrastructure. Sponsored placements are inserted into the app's purchase journey. Each ad is targeted on the retailer's profile and purchase history, so brands reach the most relevant buyers. Booking works as an auction: the advertiser pays only for the ads that are actually displayed. Brands, including third parties, build, run, and track their campaigns self-service from the Be Ads platform, with real-time performance monitoring. The business model: AB InBev, which already owns the channel and the purchase data, sells audience on its own distribution network. The foundation is large and public: BEES generated $52.5 billion in GMV in 2025 (up 12%), was live in 29 markets as of December 31, with 72% of group revenue captured through B2B digital platforms, and an audience of 3.9 million monthly active users on which the network relies. The honest caveat: no advertising revenue specific to BEES Ads is broken out publicly, and the network's mechanics are described only by the vendor Topsort.

niveau_preuve.justification: The BEES Ads mechanics (automated auction, AI personalization based on the retailer's profile and purchase history, self-service for brands, 3.9 million monthly active users) are documented by a quantified case study from the vendor Topsort, which corresponds to level B (quantified platform/vendor case study). The scale of the foundation is corroborated by an established press source (Digital Commerce 360) reporting AB InBev's 2025 annual results: $52.5B in GMV (+12%), 29 markets, 72% of revenue through B2B digital platforms. The caveat that prevents a higher rating: no advertising revenue specific to BEES Ads is broken out in a financial document, no precise launch date is published, and the description of the advertising setup rests on the vendor alone. The official AB InBev page consulted does not mention BEES Ads.

stack_technique.detail: AB InBev's B2B super app through which retailers order and restock. Serves as both the channel and the data source (profile and purchase history) for the BEES Ads network.
Auction-based retail media infrastructure that powers BEES Ads: targeting of sponsored placements, automated auction, self-service interface, and real-time campaign tracking.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Real time: sponsored placements are awarded by auction on each display in the app, brands activate or pause their campaigns whenever they want, and performance tracking is continuous.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: AB InBev's BEES Retail Media / CRM team runs the network and the advertiser relationship. Advertising brands manage their campaigns self-service. Topsort provides and operates the auction and targeting infrastructure.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The retailer's profile and purchase history on BEES: this is what targets each ad toward the relevant buyers. Without this first-party ordering data, personalization and the value of the inventory collapse.

etapes.detail: AB InBev opens sponsored placements in the BEES app's purchase journey, backed by Topsort's infrastructure.
The advertising brand builds its campaign, sets its budget and targets directly on the Be Ads platform.
On each display, the most relevant ad for the retailer is selected by auction based on its profile and purchase history; the advertiser pays only for the ads displayed.
The brand tracks performance in real time and adjusts, activates, or pauses its campaign.

prerequis_data: A proprietary digital channel with a captive audience (app, marketplace, portal) that a population returns to regularly
First-party behavioral and purchase data per user, suited to targeting placements
An identifiable inventory of placements across the journey (home, search, product page, cart)
prerequis_orga: A dedicated retail media / ad sales team, separate from brand marketing, to sell the inventory and hold the advertiser relationship
A compliance framework for the use of targeting data (GDPR if EU audience, information for business users)
Clear governance between in-house brands and third-party brands that will buy the same inventory
stack_possible: A turnkey auction-based retail media infrastructure (Topsort type) plugged into the existing app
A self-service interface for brands to build and track their campaigns
A targeting/personalization layer backed by first-party purchase data
A measurement and per-display billing module
replication.premiere_etape: Map the captive audience of the proprietary channel and the available purchase data, then identify a first pocket of sponsorable placements in the journey, before opening an auction pilot to a small panel of brands.

playbook.action: Qualify the audience of the proprietary channel (return frequency, volume, purchase data per user) and estimate the value of a targeted advertising inventory.
playbook.livrable: Diagnostic of the monetizable audience and the available targeting data.

playbook.action: Plug an auction-based retail media infrastructure into the app, with targeting backed by the retailer's profile and purchase history.
playbook.livrable: Targeted sponsored placements, awarded by auction, in the journey.

playbook.action: Open a self-service interface for brands to build, run, and track their campaigns.
playbook.livrable: Autonomous advertiser journey, from creation to real-time reporting.

playbook.action: Bill per display (payment for the ads displayed) and measure advertiser performance to retain demand.
playbook.livrable: Monetization loop with advertiser ROI measurement.

playbook.action: Expand the inventory and open it to third-party brands, framing data compliance and in-house/third-party governance.
playbook.livrable: Retail media network open beyond the group's brands.

replication.equipe: A retail media / ad sales team for inventory sales and the advertiser relationship, a data team for the first-party targeting data, a product/adtech team for integrating the auction infrastructure, and a compliance function (GDPR, information for business users) involved on an ongoing basis.

statut_vivant.note: The BEES foundation is in active growth ($52.5B in GMV in 2025, +12%, annual results published in February 2026), and AB InBev is building a dedicated retail media team (a Director, Ads Business Strategy and Development role for the BEES Retail Media and CRM team). The caveat: BEES Ads' own activity is confirmed only by the vendor Topsort, with no advertising revenue published separately.

transposable_ue.note: BEES is already deployed internationally, Europe included, so the retail media network building block is technically transposable. Two constraints frame its use in the EU. First, GDPR: personalizing placements relies on the retailer's profile and purchase history, business-customer data whose processing for advertising purposes requires a clear legal basis and clear information. Second, the AI Act imposes no strong constraint on an advertising auction of this kind, but transparency about automated targeting remains expected. The model itself (a distributor monetizing the audience of its own B2B channel) poses no specific regulatory obstacle.
